audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart read Skill/Skill/Skill/Vayne/Skill/Vayne/Vayne in both layers, contradicting the content-layer whys, which already describe Vayne winning Level 1, Sett winning Levels 2 through 6, and Vayne winning late.
audit.why: Vayne out-ranges Sett at level 1 but has no dash — Tumble is a 300-range hop against Sett's 490-range Facebreaker — so the melee bracket from level 2 to first item belongs to Sett.
audit.corrected: Vayne / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Sett / Vayne, matching the packet chart and the existing whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].why credited Sterak's Gage with making Sett 'nearly unburstable' against Vayne.
audit.why: Silver Bolts (W) deals a percentage of max health as bonus TRUE damage on every third hit, so health and resistances are the wrong purchase against her — a flagged missing interaction (resistances-invalidated).
audit.corrected: phases[6].why now states the true-damage scaling and why stacking stats does not answer it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing recorded that Tumble (Q) is an auto-attack reset, nor Condemn's real cooldown.
audit.why: Tumble carries the autoReset flag: the damage arrives on the attack wind-up, not on the cast, which is the actual cue for stepping in or out. Condemn is 20/18/16/14/12s and requires terrain behind the target to stun at all.
audit.corrected: The reset tell is now in spikes[0].text; Condemn's rank-1 20s and rank-5 12s and its wall requirement are in breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Vayne on every CS, but respect her opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Vayne's attack range and Night Hunter move speed let her chip you for free at level 1. Take the melee CS, eat nothing extra, and wait for Facebreaker at 3.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Vayne has her core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield her return damage, out.
edits.after: Vayne has no dash — Tumble (Q) is a 300-range hop. Facebreaker at 490 catches her mid-hop, and a full Grit Haymaker deletes a 550-range squishy.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Condemn and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Silver Bolts (W) is percent max health true damage, so Sterak's and armour do not save you. Land Facebreaker or you never touch her.

edits.before: - Vayne Condemn: matchup-defining — Wall-stun. E-stun her so she can’t kite. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Vayne Condemn (E): 20s at rank 1, 12s at rank 5 — the only stun she has, and it needs a wall behind you.

edits.before: She kites your all-in — E-stun to stick, all-in early. Sett wins by trading around Vayne's Condemn and cashing the pattern: e-stun to stick, all-in early.
edits.after: Vayne has no dash — only Tumble, a 300-range hop. Facebreaker at 490 out-reaches it, so all-in levels 2-6 before Silver Bolts' percent-HP true damage scales past you.

edits.before: Once you have E Facebreaker you win: pull her out of a Q Tumble reposition, W with a full Grit bar, and her Silver Bolts third-proc can't out-race your burst at melee range.
edits.after: Facebreaker (E) wins this window: Tumble (Q) is an auto reset, so the wind-up is your cue — step in as she lands it, pull her, and cash a full Grit Haymaker before her third Silver Bolt.

notes: Chart flipped in matched pairs to the packet chart; the content whys already described that chart, so only the side/rating tokens and three contradicting full-layer whys needed changing. Whether Condemn's knockback can be Flash-buffered or cleansed is not in the kit data and was not asserted.
